title: Homemade Acini di Pepe
description: Stiff semolina dough, rolled into thin ropes and cut into tiny beads.
yield: Makes enough to replace 1 cup dry

steps.do: Stir the semolina and water together with a fork until shaggy, then knead on the counter 8 to 10 minutes into a smooth, stiff dough. Add water a teaspoon at a time only if it won't come together; a firm, dry dough holds the tiny shape and doesn't smear when cut.
Wrap and rest 30 minutes at room temperature so the semolina hydrates and the dough relaxes.
Cut off a small piece, keeping the rest wrapped so it doesn't dry out. Roll it under your palms into a rope about 1/8 inch thick.

Line up a few ropes and cut them crosswise into 1/8 inch pieces with a sharp knife or bench scraper. Toss right away in semolina so they don't stick, and spread on a dusted tray. Repeat with the rest of the dough.
Use fresh, or leave uncovered on the tray, stirring now and then, until hard all the way through, about 8 to 24 hours depending on humidity.
Cook in boiling salted water or simmering soup: fresh beads take 3 to 5 minutes; dried take a few minutes longer, so start tasting at 5 minutes.

items: Fresh: keeps 1 day refrigerated in a semolina-dusted container. Or freeze on the tray, then bag; cook from frozen, adding about 1 minute.
Fully dried: keeps up to 1 month airtight at room temperature.
Italian Wedding Soup with Acini di Pepe. Stir fresh beads in for the last 5 minutes.
Hand-cut pieces are tiny cubes, not the smooth beads of store-bought. They cook and eat the same.
